part.title: OSI layers 1‑4 and encapsulation
part.script: The OSI model’s bottom four layers handle moving bits, frames, packets and transport segments across the network. Encapsulation means each lower layer wraps the data it receives with its own header, forming a new unit for the next layer.
visual_plan: Show four lower layers as a vertical stack
Illustrate encapsulation adding headers as data moves down

scenes.narration: The OSI model’s bottom four layers handle moving bits, frames, packets and transport segments across the network.
Encapsulation means each lower layer wraps the data it receives with its own header, forming a new unit for the next layer.

quick_check.question: Which statement best describes encapsulation in the OSI model?
options: Each layer removes its header before passing data up.
Each layer adds a header to data from the layer above.
Only the transport layer adds a header.
Headers are added only at the physical layer.
quick_check.explanation: Encapsulation is the process where each lower layer adds its own header to the data received from the layer above.
